title: The release dossier is a pure function over the ledger, re-measured at a sha
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). Dependency-free LEAF and the intellectual core of Gate 3: everything else in the parent is plumbing around this function.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: a PURE generator that turns the ledger reads into deterministic dossier markdown for a goal AT A GIVEN SHA, plus its durable bytes. No command kind, no PR, no UI - those are siblings.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb, gap is REAL: `grep -rn 'release\.decide|RELEASE_DOSSIER|release-dossier' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` returns ZERO (the one hit for `moe-release-handoff-binding/1` at apps/daemon/src/work/release-handoff-binding.ts:55 is the WORK handoff, unrelated - do not extend it). `packages/release` and `scripts/release` are moe-next's OWN release tooling, not the product's; do not reuse them.

THE INPUTS ALL EXIST: `/runs/read` (apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts) already carries per-node review rounds, verifier receipts, landing and publish; `POST /documents/coverage/read` (http/document-coverage-read.ts) carries per-criterion coverage - but it is keyed on the PRD contentSha256, NOT the shipping git sha, which is exactly the mismatch this row exists to close.

RE-MEASUREMENT IS THE POINT, not a detail. The dossier is built at the workspace HEAD sha, and every cited landing commit must be proven an ANCESTOR of that sha. A commit that is not an ancestor renders UNKNOWN and is LISTED - never silently dropped, because a dossier that omits what it could not verify reads as complete evidence while being incomplete. `dossier(shaA)` and `dossier(shaB)` must differ on the sha column; a generator that ignores its sha argument would pass every single-sha test.

SECTIONS: per approved criterion -> verifying node -> verifier receipt (command, exit, sha) -> landing commit sha; review rounds and refusals; the preview decision when one exists, or the explicit sentence that there is none; the installed policy revision.
definitionOfDone: A pure generator produces deterministic markdown for (goal, sha) from injected ledger reads - no store handle of its own, no clock, no git shelling inside the pure core. A golden test pins every section: the criteria table (criterion -> node -> receipt command/exit/sha -> landing sha), review rounds and refusals, the preview decision or its explicit absence, and the installed policy revision.

RE-MEASUREMENT PROVEN, both directions: a landing sha that is NOT an ancestor of the given sha renders UNKNOWN and appears in a listed section (assert the criterion id appears in the output - a dropped row is the failure being guarded); and `dossier(shaA)` differs from `dossier(shaB)` on the sha column for the same goal. The second arm is what catches a generator that ignores its sha argument.

DETERMINISM: the same inputs produce byte-identical output across two calls, and the ordering of every list is explicit (sorted by a named key), so a Map iteration order change cannot silently reorder a released dossier. Assert byte equality, not section presence.

The dossier bytes are stored durably under a versioned record (e.g. `moe-release-dossier/1`, mirroring the shape of repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts) keyed so the PR body can be re-derived and DIFFED later; a test reads the bytes back and re-derives an identical dossier.

The absent-evidence path is explicit, not empty: a goal with no preview decision states so in words; a criterion with no verifying node is listed as uncovered rather than omitted. A test asserts the words for both.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: PURE CORE. The generator takes injected reads and returns bytes; ancestry checks and store access live at the edges. A pure core is what makes the golden test meaningful and the re-derivation possible.

NEVER DROP UNMEASURABLE EVIDENCE. UNKNOWN is a rendered value, not an omission. A dossier that silently omits what it could not verify is worse than one that says so, because the reader cannot tell the difference between absent and unverified.
DO NOT reuse packages/release or scripts/release - those release moe-next itself, not the product being built. Do not extend moe-release-handoff-binding/1, which is the work-handoff record.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work; signing and hermetic verification stay out of scope.

(b) INPUT SHAPES READ.
- apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts:87-93 `SealedNode { criterionIds, dependsOn, goalRef, nodeKey, objective }`, built by `sealedNodesOf` (:94) from `graph.content.nodeAuthority.definitions` filtered by snapshot `executionBearing`. - apps/daemon/src/http/document-coverage-read.ts:265 `totals { contracts, criteria, goals, planned, requirements, unattributable, verified }`; criterion status vocabulary is PLANNED | VERIFIED | UNATTRIBUTABLE; the whole read is keyed on the PRD `contentSha256` (`coverageOf(sha, ...)`), NOT a git sha — the mismatch this row closes.
- apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:22 `VerifierExecutionInput { byteCount, outputSha256, test, workspace }`; :37 `VerifierExecutionEvidence` adds `evidenceSha256` and `exitCode: 0`. So a receipt's "command" is the `test` field and its exit is always 0 on a PASSED receipt — a non-zero verification never mints one.
- apps/daemon/src/repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts is the shape to mirror: version const + command-kind const + `hash([VERSION, "receipt-id", ...parts])` deterministic id (`landingReceiptId` :126) + aggregate id helper (:120) + exact-key decoder that re-derives the id and refuses on mismatch + `freezeDeep`. Its store side is repository/landing-ledger.ts: `store.commitExpectedVersionDecision({ commandKind, committedResultBytes, correlationId, decidedAt, events, expectedVersion, key:{commandId,principalId,projectId}, requestBytes, targetAggregateId })`, read back via `store.getCommandDecision` + re-decode. `.js` bridges are the convention in that directory (`export * from "./landing-receipt-contracts.ts";`) — 7 of them exist; missing bridge = ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND at boot.
- Real-store test harness: `openStore`/`closeStores`/`hex64`/`PROJECT_ID` from ../review/review-test-fixtures.js (used by repository/landing-ledger.test.ts).

(c) ANCESTRY SEAM: NO HELPER EXISTS. `grep -rnE 'merge-base|isAncestor|rev-list --contains|--is-ancestor' --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src` => ZERO. Port shape to follow is `GitRunner` at repository/git-landing-port.ts:65: `(cwd, args: readonly string[], stdin?) => Promise<{ code: number|null; stderr; stdout }>`, consumed by bootstrap/activation-receipts-ports.ts:40 as a `readonly git: GitRunner` field.

GIT INVOCATION CHOSEN: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <landingSha> <sha>` in the workspace. WHY: it is the only plumbing that answers ancestry with an EXIT CODE rather than parsed stdout, and its three outcomes map exactly onto the three verdicts this row needs — code 0 = ANCESTOR, code 1 = NOT_ANCESTOR, anything else (128 for an unknown/ambiguous object, null for a spawn failure or the 60s timeout) = UNMEASURABLE. Rejected `rev-list --contains`: it answers "which refs contain", needs stdout parsing, and prints nothing for both "not contained" and "bad object", collapsing NOT_ANCESTOR into UNMEASURABLE — precisely the distinction this row's DoD asserts on. Rejected plain `merge-base <a> <b>` + string compare: two git facts and a comparison where one exit code suffices.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN: `merge-base --is-ancestor` is async through `GitRunner`, but the pure core must be sync to be byte-deterministic and fakeable. So the seam is split — the pure generator takes a SYNC predicate `(commitSha) => "ANCESTOR"|"NOT_ANCESTOR"|"UNMEASURABLE"`, and an edge resolver pre-resolves every cited commit through the async GitRunner into a lookup the sync predicate closes over. That keeps zero git shelling inside the core (task rail 1) and makes the golden test a pure data test.

implementationPlan.description: THE PURE GENERATOR, in a new apps/daemon/src/release/release-dossier.ts. It takes the folded ledger facts plus a sha plus an injected ancestry predicate, and returns deterministic markdown bytes. NO store handle, NO clock, NO git shelling inside the core — that is what makes the golden test meaningful and the later re-derivation possible. Sections: per approved criterion -> verifying node -> verifier receipt (command, exit, sha) -> landing commit sha; review rounds and refusals; the preview decision or the explicit sentence that there is none; the installed policy revision. EVERY LIST IS SORTED BY A NAMED KEY — state which in a comment — so a Map iteration order change cannot silently reorder a released dossier. Keep it under 250 lines; if the section renderers push past that, split them into a sibling module rather than growing one file.
implementationPlan.note:
PURE GENERATOR LANDED. `renderReleaseDossier(input: DossierInput, sha: string, ancestry: AncestryPredicate): string`.

SPLIT AS THE STEP DIRECTED. First draft was 264 lines — over the step's 250 target — so the section renderers moved to a sibling rather than the file growing. Final: release-dossier.ts 166, release-dossier-sections.ts 117, release-dossier-contracts.ts 181. Dependency runs ONE WAY (release-dossier.ts -> release-dossier-sections.ts -> release-dossier-contracts.ts, no cycle); `DossierGap`/`DossierGapCode`/`CriterionRow` are re-exported from release-dossier.ts so consumers keep a single import site. Both new modules ship `.js` bridges.

PURITY HELD: the core imports nothing but its own contracts and section renderers. No store handle, no `Date`, no `node:child_process`, no git. Verified by grep on the two modules: zero matches for `import .* from "node:`, `Date`, `store`, `execFile`, `spawn`.

SECTIONS, in order: header (goal, project, `Re-measured at sha: <sha>`, record version) / `## Acceptance criteria` (7-column table: Criterion | Title | Node | Verifier command | Exit | Receipt sha | Landing sha) / `## Unverified evidence` / `## Review rounds` (Node | Round | Outcome | Refusal code) / `## Preview decision` / `## Installed policy`.

NAMED SORT KEYS (stated in the module JSDoc, DoD clause 3): criteria by `criterionId`; gaps by `criterionId` then `code`; review rounds by `nodeKey` then `round`. All three via `[...list].sort(...)` on a copy — the input arrays are never mutated, so a caller's ordering cannot leak in and a second call cannot observe a re-sorted input. Nothing renders in Map iteration order; the only Map (`nodes`) is a lookup, never iterated for output.

STABLE GAP CODES (global rail 1 — the tests assert the CODE, not just "UNKNOWN appeared"): CRITERION_UNCOVERED, LANDING_ABSENT, LANDING_NOT_ANCESTOR, LANDING_UNMEASURABLE, RECEIPT_ABSENT, RECEIPT_SHARED_NODE. Each has a sentence in `GAP_SENTENCES`, and every gap row carries its CRITERION ID — so an unmeasurable landing is findable BY CRITERION in the listed section, which is exactly the step-5(a) assertion (a test that only greps for "UNKNOWN somewhere" passes on a dossier that dropped the row).

NOT_ANCESTOR AND UNMEASURABLE ARE KEPT DISTINCT and are separate codes, because "we checked and it is absent" and "git would not answer" are different claims to a release reader. Both render the cell as UNKNOWN; only the code and sentence differ. The NOT_ANCESTOR/UNMEASURABLE details append the offending sha in parentheses, so the reader can go look.

`memoized()` wraps the injected predicate: at most ONE consultation per distinct cited commit (step 5c), and a THROWN predicate is caught and becomes UNMEASURABLE -> UNKNOWN, so an unreachable git cannot take the dossier down.

GAPS ARE A LIST, NOT A FIELD. A criterion with both an absent receipt AND a non-ancestor landing emits BOTH rows. A singular `gap` would have silently dropped the second — the exact failure class this row exists to prevent.

`cell()` escapes `|` and collapses newlines: a verifier command is a real command line and an unescaped pipe would break the table row (and could forge a column).

GATE: `pnpm typecheck` exit 0, `apps/daemon typecheck: Done`. Tests land in step 4.

implementationPlan.description: THE GOLDEN TEST AND DETERMINISM, in a new apps/daemon/src/release/release-dossier.test.ts. (a) A golden pins every section for a representative goal — the criteria table with node / receipt command / exit / sha / landing sha, the review rounds and refusals, the preview decision, the policy revision. (b) DETERMINISM: the same inputs produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output across two calls — assert byte equality, not section presence, since a section-presence assertion passes while the order drifts. (c) THE ABSENT-EVIDENCE PATHS, in words rather than blanks: a goal with NO preview decision states so; a criterion with NO verifying node is LISTED as uncovered rather than omitted. Assert the sentences — an omitted row and a covered row are indistinguishable to a reader, which is the whole failure this row guards against.
implementationPlan.note:
GOLDEN + DETERMINISM + ABSENT-EVIDENCE LANDED. 10 tests, all passing.

GATE (targeted, standalone, foreground): `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release` from apps/daemon => `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  10 passed (10)`, exit 0. NONZERO executed count line quoted (global rail 8).

NOTE ON THE FILTER (global rail 8 / prior knowledge confirmed again): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test -- release-dossier` does NOT filter — vitest ran the WHOLE package (`Test Files 416 passed (417)`, `Tests 8324 passed (8325)`). The `--` reaches vitest but the preceding `src` positional already matched everything. Targeted daemon runs need `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json <dir>` directly.

(a) THE GOLDEN pins every section BYTE-FOR-BYTE with a single `toBe` against a hand-written expected document — heading presence is never asserted, because a presence assertion stays green while order drifts and a dossier that reorders between renderings cannot be diffed. Pinned: the header (goal, project, `Re-measured at sha`, record version), the 7-column criteria table with node / verifier command / exit / receipt sha / landing sha, the `## Unverified evidence` table, review rounds with their refusal codes, the preview decision's four lines, the policy revision line.

THE FIXTURE SUPPLIES BOTH LISTS OUT OF SORTED ORDER ON PURPOSE (criteria as charlie/alpha/bravo, rounds as bravo#1/alpha#1/bravo#2), so a generator that rendered input order would fail the golden rather than pass it by accident. A second test PINS THAT PREMISE explicitly (`toStrictEqual` on the fixture's raw order) before asserting rendered order — otherwise a later fixture tidy-up would silently make the sort assertion vacuous.

(b) DETERMINISM asserted as BYTES, not strings: `Buffer.from(a,"utf8").equals(Buffer.from(b,"utf8"))` across two calls. Plus a NON-MUTATION arm — the generator sorts copies, so the caller's arrays are unchanged after a render and a second render cannot observe a re-sorted input. That arm is what stops an in-place `.sort()` from making "two calls agree" true for the wrong reason.

DETERMINISM HARDENING FOUND WHILE WRITING THE TEST — the comparators were `String.prototype.localeCompare`, which is ICU/locale-sensitive (it orders `-`, `_` and case differently from code units, and differs between locales). Two hosts would then render the same facts in a different order and defeat the diffing the stored bytes exist for. Replaced with an explicit `byCodeUnit` comparator in release-dossier-sections.ts, used by all three sorts, with the reason in its JSDoc.

(c) ABSENT EVIDENCE IN WORDS, six arms, each asserting the SENTENCE or the STABLE CODE (global rail 1), never merely that something was missing: no preview => `There is no preview decision for this goal.` AND the positive-case line is asserted absent; an uncovered criterion => its id appears in BOTH the criteria table and the listed gap row `| crit-charlie | CRITERION_UNCOVERED | ... |` (a dropped row is the failure guarded, so the assertion is on the ID, not on "UNKNOWN appears somewhere"); a criterion naming a node that is not execution-bearing => the gap detail names the missing key; empty criteria / rounds / policy => their three sentences; a landed node with no receipt => `RECEIPT_ABSENT` with the landing sha still rendered; and a node with NEITHER receipt NOR landing emits BOTH `RECEIPT_ABSENT` and `LANDING_ABSENT` rows — the arm that proves gaps are a LIST and a second gap is not silently dropped.

implementationPlan.description: RE-MEASUREMENT, BOTH DIRECTIONS — the clause that makes this a dossier rather than a report. (a) A landing sha that is NOT an ancestor of the given sha renders UNKNOWN and appears in a LISTED section: assert the criterion id appears in the output, because a dropped row is exactly the failure being guarded and a test that only checks 'UNKNOWN appears somewhere' passes on a dossier that dropped the row and printed UNKNOWN elsewhere. (b) `dossier(shaA)` DIFFERS from `dossier(shaB)` for the same goal on the sha column — this is what catches a generator that accepts a sha argument and ignores it, which would otherwise pass every single-sha test in the file. (c) The ancestry predicate is consulted ONCE PER CITED COMMIT and its refusal (a git failure, not a false answer) renders UNKNOWN rather than throwing — an unreachable git must not take the dossier down.
implementationPlan.note:
RE-MEASUREMENT ARMS LANDED, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Suite now 16 tests. Gate: `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release` from apps/daemon => `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  16 passed (16)`, exit 0.

(a) NOT-AN-ANCESTOR RENDERS UNKNOWN AND IS LISTED. Test "renders UNKNOWN and LISTS the criterion when its landing is not an ancestor" asserts the CRITERION ID inside the gap row — `| crit-orphan | LANDING_NOT_ANCESTOR | the cited landing commit is not an ancestor of this sha (<sha>) |` — not merely that UNKNOWN appears somewhere, because that weaker assertion passes on a dossier that DROPPED the row and printed UNKNOWN in an unrelated cell. Two further assertions close the loop: the landing CELL is UNKNOWN, and `expect(rendered).not.toContain("| <ORPHAN_LANDING> |")` proves the unverified sha is never presented anywhere as evidence.

(b) TWO SHAS DIFFER, in two arms of increasing strength. The first pins the column directly: same input, two shas, `bytes(atHead).equals(bytes(atOther))` is FALSE, each output contains its own `- Re-measured at sha: <sha>` and `not.toContain` the other. The second models what the real edge does — the production predicate closes over the sha, so the SAME landing is an ancestor at one sha and NOT at the other; the evidence column must follow the SHA, not the ledger. At HEAD_SHA the landing renders and the section says "Every cited commit was re-measured as an ancestor of this sha."; at OTHER_SHA the same landing is gone from the table and `| crit-alpha | LANDING_NOT_ANCESTOR |` appears.

(c) ONCE PER CITED COMMIT, AND A FAILING PORT DOES NOT THROW. Three criteria over two distinct cited commits => `expect(calls).toStrictEqual([ALPHA_LANDING, BRAVO_LANDING])` — the exact call log, so a per-criterion re-consultation (three calls) is caught, not just a wrong total. A predicate that THROWS (`fatal: not a git repository`) renders `LANDING_UNMEASURABLE` with the sha in the detail, asserts `not.toContain` LANDING_NOT_ANCESTOR (the two are distinct codes: "could not check" is not "checked and absent"), and the render returns normally. A final arm proves the UNMEASURABLE verdict is CACHED too — two criteria on one failing commit consult git ONCE — so an unreachable git is not re-spawned per criterion.

DRILLS (global rail 1 + 13). Both mutated modules are UNTRACKED (`git status --porcelain apps/daemon/src/release/` => `?? apps/daemon/src/release/`), so `git diff` is blind to them and CANNOT serve as restore proof. Out-of-tree backups taken in %TEMP%/drill-worker-12c76c19 before drilling; each restore proven by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore.

DRILL 1 — generator ignores its sha argument (`- Re-measured at sha: ${sha}` -> a constant). Step-5(b) arm went RED: `× differs on the sha column for the same goal at two different shas`. Result `Tests  3 failed | 13 passed (16)` (the golden and the sha-dependent re-measure arm also pin the sha, so they went red too — expected).
